text:
The Red Wings' season has been defined by a player who isn't playing. Dylan Larkin asked for a trade, refused to report, and was suspended without pay, according to multiple reports, and his camp has declined to widen his ten-team list. The Wild have been named as pushing hard (The Athletic's Michael Russo), the Bruins linked, and nothing has moved. Every week this drags on, Detroit plays without its best center and without an answer.

Then John Gibson went down with an upper-body injury, and Michal Postava was recalled under emergency conditions. The Red Wings are 7-8-3, winless in three after a 4-0 loss in Colorado, and our simulations give them a 23 percent playoff chance.

Here's the strange part: the process is decent. Detroit takes 53 percent of the five-on-five expected goals and has scored 11 fewer goals than its chances say it should, a finishing gap that big rarely lasts. Viktor Arvidsson has been the best news, a hat trick against Chicago and a line with Alex DeBrincat and Emmitt Finnie that drives play. Our read: this team is better than its record and worse than its situation. The Larkin resolution, whenever it comes, decides which one wins out.
headline: Detroit without its captain, and now without its starter
